steps.explanationAfterStep: The enolate is one ion with its negative charge shared by the α-carbon and oxygen; this drawing puts it on oxygen, the major contributor. Only a small fraction of acetone is deprotonated at any moment: water (pKa 15.7) is a stronger acid than acetone (pKa about 20).
Protonation on oxygen gives the enol and gives back hydroxide, so the base is a catalyst. In base the order is the reverse of acid catalysis: the C–H breaks first, then the oxygen gains its proton.

title: Base-catalysed enolisation of acetone
subtitle: Through the enolate: off carbon, back on oxygen
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 20

enol.caption: prop-1-en-2-ol (the enol of acetone) + hydroxide + water

enolate.caption: the enolate + two water molecules
hintTiers: The enolate has negative charge on oxygen and on the α-carbon. Which end gives the enol when it takes a proton?
The enolate oxygen takes a proton from a water molecule. Two arrows.
Enolate oxygen lone pair → a hydrogen of water; that O–H bond of water → a lone pair on its oxygen.
enolate.learnerPrompt: Water is the acid now. Protonate the enolate on oxygen to give the enol.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Protonating the carbon gives back acetone. That does happen, and the ketone wins at equilibrium, but the question asks for the enol: put the proton on oxygen.
The oxygen of water is electron-rich. The enolate takes a proton, the δ+ hydrogen of water.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: the enolate oxygen takes the proton. The hydrogen now has two bonds: break its bond to the water oxygen.

reactants.caption: acetone + hydroxide + water
hintTiers: A C–H next to a C=O group is acidic (pKa about 20). Why is its conjugate base stabilised?
Hydroxide takes the drawn α-hydrogen. The C–H electrons form a C=C bond and the C=O π electrons move onto oxygen. Three arrows.
Hydroxide lone pair → the drawn α-hydrogen; that C–H bond → a π bond to the carbonyl carbon; the C=O π bond → a lone pair on the carbonyl oxygen.
reactants.learnerPrompt: Hydroxide is the base. Form the enolate.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Hydroxide can add to the carbonyl carbon, but the hydrate it gives is a reversible dead end. Here hydroxide acts as a base on an α-hydrogen.
Hydroxide taking a proton from water just swaps one hydroxide for another. Look for the acidic C–H of acetone.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Good: the base takes the proton and a C=C forms. The carbonyl carbon now has five bonds: move the C=O π electrons onto oxygen.

mechanismSummary: Hydroxide removes an α-proton, giving the enolate. Water then protonates the enolate on oxygen: the enol. A hydrogen has moved from carbon to oxygen, with hydroxide regenerated. Acid and base both catalyse enolisation, in opposite orders: in acid the oxygen is protonated first; in base the α-carbon is deprotonated first. Protonation on carbon instead gives back the ketone, which is far more stable.
